body_excerpt: Usage metrics API adds usage from tools like OpenCode - GitHub Changelog Skip to content Skip to sidebar / Blog Changelog Docs Customer stories Try GitHub Copilot app Attend GitHub Universe Search Changelog Docs Customer stories Attend GitHub Universe Try GitHub Copilot app Back to changelog Improvement October 23, 2026 • 2 minute read Usage metrics API adds usage from tools like OpenCode Table of Contents What's new Why this matters Important notes Menu. Currently selected: What's new What's new Why this matters Important notes The Copilot usage metrics API now reports model usage from more of the tools your developers use with Copilot, including tools like OpenCode that weren’t previously captured in your reports. A new totals_by_client array is available in the enterprise, organization, enterprise-user, and organization-user 1-day and 28-day reports. What’s new Each totals_by_client entry represents one client and includes: client : The tool that sent the requests, such as opencode , claude_code , codex , zed , copilot_cli , github_app , cloud_agent , code_review , vscode , or jetbrains . Unrecognized clients are grouped under other . request_count : The number of successful model requests from the client. session_count : The number of distinct sessions from the client. token_usage : Prompt tokens, output tokens, and average tokens per request. totals_by_model : The same request and token metrics broken down by model, with a model_selection_mode that shows whether the model was requested directly ( user_selected ), chosen by auto ( auto ), or chosen by the product ( product_selected ). Selection modes that aren’t reported individually yet appear as other , and values that can’t be normalized appear as unknown . Why this matters More developers now use Copilot as the model provider behind tools outside the IDE. Because those tools often don’t send editor telemetry, their usage was missing from totals_by_ide and hard to account for. Counting requests on the server

Currently selected: Turn an issue notification into a pull request Turn an issue notification into a pull request Get started The new GitHub app in Teams brings notifications and Copilot together, helping teams turn issues into fixes and ship code faster without leaving the conversation. Get notified in channels, group chats, or private chats, then @mention GitHub to turn updates into action. Turn an issue notification into a pull request Get notified: A bug report arrives in Teams. Take action: @github investigates the issue, fixes the bug, and creates a pull request. Review and ship: Your team reviews, tests, and merges the fix. Get started Explore the new GitHub app in Microsoft Teams , previously called GitHub notifications. If you already have GitHub notifications installed, update the app to the latest version. Your existing notification capabilities will continue to work. If you use the legacy GitHub app, which will be renamed “GitHub (deprecated)” and retired on November 16, install the consolidated GitHub app using the link above to continue using Copilot in Teams. In the consolidated app, mention @GitHub and follow any prompts to connect your GitHub account and select a repository. Join the discussion within the GitHub Community . title: Document mentions, Cmd+K actions, and a fresh look for ChatPRD | ChatPRD Blog
author: Claire Vo
excerpt: Attach ChatPRD docs with @, take action with Cmd+K, explore the refreshed design, and connect your favorite AI tools. Plus Claude Duet and video-editing workflows.
body_excerpt: Document mentions, Cmd+K actions, and a fresh look for ChatPRD | ChatPRD Blog Open menu Product Enterprise Customers Pricing Resources Reviews How I AI Log in Get a demo Start free ← All articles Back / Document mentions, Cmd+K actions, and a fresh look for ChatPRD Document mentions, Cmd+K actions, and a fresh look for ChatPRD Attach ChatPRD docs with @, take action with Cmd+K, explore the refreshed design, and connect your favorite AI tools. Plus Claude Duet and video-editing workflows. Claire Vo October 23, 2026 · 3 min read Happy Friday! A few fun updates to make it easier to work with what you've already written. Bring other ChatPRD docs into a chat, tell Cmd+K what you want to do, and find the right setup for your favorite AI tools. Plus, ChatPRD has a fresh new look! Let's jump in 🥳 📎 Bring your other docs into the conversation Working on something that builds on another PRD? Type @ in the chat box to find and attach your ChatPRD docs . They'll stay in the chat's document list so you can come back to them. ChatPRD can also search for relevant docs on its own, starting with your project, and link the docs it mentions. Try asking it to check whether your launch brief lines up with your pricing PRD. Bring a doc into your next chat → ⌘ Tell Cmd+K what you want to do Open Cmd+K (Ctrl+K on Windows) and try “turn the onboarding checklist PRD into a prototype.” ChatPRD suggests an action and the doc to use. Press Enter to continue in chat with an editable draft, or choose Send now to get started right away. You can also use it to brainstorm, research, open or pin a chat, and jump to settings. One request, one action. 🎨 A fresh coat of pink We've brought the ChatPRD website's colors into the app, with a coral, pink, and violet gradient on the home screen and a little more pink throughout. Come take a look! 🔌 Find ChatPRD in your favorite AI tools We've updated Settings → Integrations → MCP with setup for ChatGPT, Cursor, Grok Bot, Codex, Claude Code, Claude, and more.
